definitions: A classification of streptococcal bacteria, specifically Streptococcus agalactiae, known to cause serious infections in newborns and sometimes in adults.
A category in rallying, active from 1982 to 1986, that allowed for a limited number of highly modified, high-performance cars.
examples: Screening for Group B strep is routine during pregnancy.
The Group B era of rallying produced some of the most iconic cars.
